note: Adapted from Sands' (1972) species-level description of Anenteotermes cicur, originally in English; the species is soldierless; in the comparisons of the original the spelling of the similar species is inconsistent in the OCR (improelatans and improcinctus both occur), so the relevant sentences retain only the morphological differences and omit the species names; measurement-table headings, figure numbers, type locality and biological records are not translated, and numbers in the tables partly destroyed by OCR are omitted.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Among the alates, only three species have the posterior part of the head (behind the compound eyes) unevenly rounded, and the present species is one of them. In the other similar species the constriction of the meso- and metathorax is broader, the apical mandibular teeth are longer and the first marginal tooth of the right mandible is longer than the second. The worker has been compared with A. amachetus and A. ateuchestes; its enteric valve lacks appendages and thus differs from A. cnaphorus, A. nanus and A. polyscolus; it is also stated that the form in which the anterior margins of the first and second marginal teeth of the right mandible are equal and the mixed segment very short differs from the present species, that the form with the shorter mixed segment is larger and has a less swollen postclypeus, that another smaller species has longer apical mandibular teeth, and that A. disluctans has inconspicuous cephalic setae. The worker abdomen is not strongly dehiscent; about a quarter of the preserved specimens are ruptured.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule pale yellow, pilosity yellow, setae rather numerous but not dense. Postclypeus moderately swollen, Pcl/W 0.28, Pcl/Ri 1.79. Apical teeth of the mandibles short, La/Li 0.46, Ra/Ri 0.58; accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible just clear of the molar prominence in surface view, composite ratio 9.15; first marginal tooth of the right mandible distinctly behind the line from the apical tooth to the second marginal tooth, its anterior margin about half that of the second, composite ratio 13.52. Anterior tibia weakly swollen, T1/Tw 4.12, the third apical spur about half the length of the other two spurs. Overlap of midgut and hindgut about four times the width of the midgut at the origin of the Malpighian tubules; enteric valve seat with three very weak lobes, connected by a distinct neck to the second paunch, lateral in the unopened abdomen; endopads of the enteric valve all retracted, of roughly equal development, the surface scaly; membranous wall of the valve between and outside the pads with sparse minute spines.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule dark brown, darker above the ocelli; fontanelle about half an ocellus, oval, slightly concave, pale brown; central spot short-oval, about half the fontanelle, slightly raised into a small tubercle, visible in profile, dark brown; postclypeus dark brown, labrum brown; frontal mark a flat dark brown crescent; antennae yellowish brown. Pronotum dark brown; meso- and metanotum brown, the mesothoracic transverse suture absent, the metathoracic one weakly developed; femora and tibiae pale yellowish brown, tarsi yellow. Abdominal tergites dark brown, dorsal spiracles darker; sternites yellowish brown, paler medially, ventral spiracles dark brown; cerci yellow. Posterior margin of the head capsule faintly sinuate, not evenly rounded; ocelli medium-sized, the distance to the compound eye half to two thirds of their own minimum diameter; postclypeus weakly swollen, Pcl/W 0.25–0.26, the posterior margin rather indistinct, broadly rounded, median suture almost effaced; apical teeth of the mandibles short, La/Li 0.49–0.50, Ra/Ri 0.70; accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible just clear of the molar prominence, composite ratio 6.73–7.33; first marginal tooth of the right mandible slightly behind the line from the apical tooth to the second marginal tooth, the anterior margins of the marginal teeth about equal, composite ratio 21.6–22.9. Pilosity of the head capsule uneven, brown, not felted.
